# Mapping Sets

<!-- purpose: Where Mapping Sets files live, the kinds they hold and every key they accept -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

Data type mapping sets, one file each under `data_types/mapping_sets/`. A set pairs each application type — the physical view of a signal, with its unit, its conversion and its range — with the implementation type that stores it, and a component names the sets its behaviour maps with. Every application type or enumeration a component's ports speak in has to be paired in one of them, because generated code needs to know what stores it. The directory is mandatory and may be empty: a project whose interfaces are typed by implementation types alone needs no set.

One file per `mapping_set`, in `data_types/mapping_sets/` under the model root, named after its `name` and ending in `.yaml`. Where that file name is already taken by another element's file — compared without regard to case — the file gets the nearest free `~1`, `~2`, … instead; the element is identified by the `name` inside the file, never by its file name.

## `mapping_set` { #mapping_set }

<!-- purpose: Writing `mapping_set` files in Mapping Sets: each key, its type and default -->

One mapping set, emitted as a `DATA-TYPE-MAPPING-SET`. It holds the pairs that say which implementation type stores each application type. A component references the set as a whole, so one set serves every component that names it, and a project is free to keep one set for the whole model or one per domain.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The set's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/mapping_sets/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be blank, and immutable. |
| `maps` | a list of `map` blocks | no | `[]` | The pairs the set declares, addressed by the application type each one maps, which appears at most once in a set. The order is the model's and is the order the pairs are emitted in. An empty list is legal and declares nothing. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the set. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/MappingSets`, its layer's package, this mapping set is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the mapping set and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/MappingSets/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/MappingSets` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/MappingSets/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/MappingSets` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |

## Blocks used inside those files { #blocks-used-inside-those-files }

<!-- purpose: The blocks nested inside Mapping Sets files, which are not files of their own -->

These are not files of their own: each appears as a block inside an element of this layer.

### `map` { #map }

<!-- purpose: Writing `map` blocks in Mapping Sets: each key, its type and default -->

One pair: the application type, and the implementation type that stores it. Both sides name a declared data type by its own name; which kinds each side may name is checked across files, because the answer is in the type's own file and not here.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string, the `name` of [application_types](application_types.md) | yes | — | The name of the declared application type, enumeration, record or array this pair maps, an element of the `application_types` layer. It is the pair's identity inside the set, and so immutable. |
| `implementation` | string, the `name` of [implementation_types](implementation_types.md) | yes | — | The name of the declared value type, reference type, implementation record or implementation array that stores it, and never a pointer. Repointing the pair at another implementation type edits this field; pairing a different application type is a different pair. |
